clue.text: No Chartism reforms for him!

indicators.note: reforms means the letters of No Chartism are remade into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cry that a political reformer's programme holds nothing for a certain kind of traditionalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reforms' rearranges NO CHARTISM. The whole clue is also the definition: the Chartists campaigned for democratic reform, so a supporter of the crown would want none of it. Chartism was a 19th-century British working-class movement for voting rights.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of rule by king or queen would naturally oppose a radical democratic movement.

clue.text: Navy's not in recent fashion

indicators.note: not in tells us the navy's letters are absent from the word for recent

parts.note: recent means modern
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A remark that the navy is out of step with current fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a prevailing style or fashion, as in 'the latest mode'.

clue.text: Criminal set up traps crazy one of no fixed abode

indicators.note: traps means one piece closes around the others
set up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, i.e. reversed

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
crazy means mad
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A criminal sets up traps for a crazed homeless drifter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' reads the criminal upwards, as this is a down clue; 'traps' then encloses the crazy one.
explanation.definitionFit: A wandering person who moves from place to place has no permanent home, the adjective's very sense.

clue.text: Scrummaging around Belgium and Swiss city looking like a tourist

indicators.note: around means the scrummaging word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: rucking is scrummaging for the ball in rugby
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
Berne is the Swiss capital

explanation.surface: Rugby players scrum in Belgium and Switzerland, gawping like visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' has the scrummaging word wrap the Belgian and Swiss pieces. In rugby a ruck is a loose scrum over the ball on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Craning one's neck to gawp at sights is typical behaviour of a sightseeing visitor.

clue.text: He struck awkward aggressive salesman

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters of he struck are clumsily jumbled

explanation.surface: A man lashed out clumsily at a pushy salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: A huckster is a pushy, often dishonest peddler who sells aggressively.

clue.text: Promise after the heart of Russell Brand

indicators.note: after places the promise word behind the picked letter
the heart of picks the central letter of Russell

parts.note: one's word is a promise

explanation.surface: A promise made after the heart of comedian Russell Brand.
explanation.walkthrough: Russell Brand, the comedian, is a red herring: 'Brand' is the definition, an old word for a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: Brand is a poetic or archaic term for a blade, from a flaming torch's gleam.

clue.text: Boast about what one wears

indicators.note: about here means turned about, so the boasting word reads backwards

parts.note: to brag is to boast

explanation.surface: Someone bragging about their clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, particularly a distinctive style of dress.

clue.text: One hour in work place bustling with activity

parts.note: an means one, as in 'an apple'

indicators.note: in places the hour letter inside the word for work

parts.note: to till is to work the soil

explanation.surface: An hour spent at a busy workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: An ants' nest mound swarms with busy insects, so it stands for any place full of activity.

clue.text: Pub encouraged the Spanish to be entertained with shorts

indicators.note: to be entertained means the Spanish article is taken inside the other pieces

parts.note: a bar is a pub
egged on means encouraged
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A pub urged on a Spaniard to enjoy themselves in shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be entertained' puts the Spanish article inside the pub-plus-encouraged pair, splitting them.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing shorts leaves one's legs uncovered.

clue.text: After March Bishop gets release from army

indicators.note: After places the bishop letter behind the march word

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop is discharged from the army after a march.
explanation.definitionFit: Demob is short for demobilisation, the discharge of soldiers from service.

clue.text: Rhetoric's out of order though he makes his voice heard

indicators.note: out of order means the letters are put into a different sequence

parts.note: the 's here supplies an S to the letters

explanation.surface: A speaker's rhetoric is out of line, though at least he gets heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir singer uses his voice to be heard; a playful description of singing.

clue.text: When a person lived unhurriedly

explanation.surface: Taking it easy throughout one's life.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both during one's lifetime and at one's leisure, without hurry.

clue.text: Dashing steeds right in exercise got up to impress

indicators.note: in places the anagram and the right word inside the exercise word

parts.note: drill is exercise, as in military drill

indicators.note: Dashing suggests the steeds charge about, so their letters are scattered

parts.note: OK means all right

explanation.surface: Horses galloping during an exercise, all decked out for show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashing' rearranges the steeds into ESSEDT, which with 'right' goes inside the exercise word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dressed to kill means wearing showy clothes meant to impress; 'got up' is dressed.

clue.text: Bold miss dances in bars

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bold type
to lack is to miss
balls are formal dances

explanation.surface: A daring young woman dancing in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a young woman and 'bars' like pubs; bars is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To vote against a candidate's admission, originally with a dark ball, is to exclude or ban them.

clue.text: Host bugs new clock

parts.note: lice are bugs
to clock is slang for to see or notice

explanation.surface: A host discovers a bug-infested new clock.
explanation.walkthrough: A licensee is the landlord of a British pub, licensed to sell alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: The holder of a pub's drinks licence is the landlord who plays host to customers.

clue.text: Jake perhaps — high flyer loses one in family film

indicators.note: in places the shortened bird inside the film rating

parts.note: PG (parental guidance) is the rating for a family film

indicators.note: loses means one letter is dropped from the bird

parts.note: an eagle soars high
A is one

explanation.surface: Someone named Jake, a high flyer, suffers a loss in a family film.
explanation.walkthrough: Jake the Peg is a comic song character with an extra leg, from Australian entertainer Rolf Harris; 'perhaps' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Jake the Peg is a novelty-song figure with a third wooden-style leg, hence an example.

clue.text: Damaged one commoner getting exposed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
an MP sits in the House of Commons
aired means exposed to view or the air

explanation.surface: One ordinary person is hurt by being exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commoner' suggests a non-aristocrat but means a Member of Parliament in the Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impaired has been weakened or harmed, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Footballer right in place for medical examination

indicators.note: in places the right letter inside the examination couch

parts.note: a doctor examines a patient on a couch

explanation.surface: A footballer receives the right treatment on the physio's examination table.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Crouch is a tall former England striker.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Crouch is a famous English footballer, so the surname is an example.

clue.text: Senior sold steroids taken internally

indicators.note: taken internally means the letters are found inside sold steroids

explanation.surface: An elderly person sold steroids that were swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: An old person is a senior citizen; a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Suave fellow gets a refreshing drink

explanation.surface: A charming man orders something cool to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a slick, ingratiating man and a thick blended fruit beverage.

clue.text: Long-haired girl's engagement announced

indicators.note: announced means the words are spoken, so we go by sound

parts.note: a girl's engagement is her suit, as in a suitor's courtship of her

explanation.surface: News of a long-haired girl getting engaged.
explanation.walkthrough: A suit is an old word for courtship or wooing; 'her suit' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hirsute means hairy or shaggy, applied to someone with abundant hair.

clue.text: Doctor remedies bad case of nauseation showing this?

definitions.text: Doctor remedies bad case of nauseation showing this?

indicators.note: Doctor as a verb means to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged
case of takes the outer letters of nauseation

explanation.surface: A doctor treating a bad bout of sickness displays a good manner with patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges REMEDIES, BAD and NN (the outside of nauseation). The whole clue also describes a GP's tactful way with patients.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's reassuring manner with patients is what a physician treating sickness would show.

clue.text: Go into mall in America topless

indicators.note: topless in a down clue means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a shopping center, American spelling

explanation.surface: Walking into an American shopping mall without a top on.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a place is to go into it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Endlessly contemplate sexy man

indicators.note: Endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to study is to contemplate

explanation.surface: Someone forever gazing at an attractive man.
explanation.definitionFit: Stud is slang for a virile, sexually attractive man.

clue.text: Lawyer: I got trial arranged

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of I got trial are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A lawyer boasting that they set up a court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A litigator is a lawyer who specialises in lawsuits and court cases.

clue.text: Northern people know instinctively when temperature's dropped

indicators.note: dropped means the temperature letter is removed

parts.note: to intuit is to know by instinct
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Arctic folk can sense when the temperature falls.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one T of INTUIT goes; the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are the indigenous peoples of Arctic Canada, Greenland and Alaska.

clue.text: Island needs second boat

parts.note: Noah's ark was a boat

explanation.surface: Reaching an island requires a second vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark is one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Sark is a small car-free Channel Island near Guernsey.

clue.text: Card game's principal advanced position

parts.note: bridge is a card game
a head is a school principal

explanation.surface: The main point of a card game is pushing forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridgehead is a forward military foothold seized in enemy territory.
